questions.question: Which of the following is the main reason a restaurant's purchasing manager should avoid buying far more fresh produce than the kitchen can use:

options.A: Large orders always cost more per item
options.B: Produce can't be stored at all
options.D: Extra produce may spoil and waste money

questions.explanation: Extra produce may spoil and waste money. Fresh produce spoils quickly, so buying too much leads to waste and higher food costs. Good purchasing balances having enough on hand with avoiding excess. Suppliers generally welcome large orders, and produce can be stored for short periods under proper refrigeration. Large orders often cost less per item, which is exactly why buyers are tempted to over-order, but the savings disappear if the produce spoils before it is used. Many restaurants order fresh items several times a week for this reason.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature and scope of purchasing

questions.question: When a hotel stores guests' credit card numbers, it should

options.A: keep the numbers in a paper notebook.
options.B: email the numbers to managers daily.
options.C: post the numbers on a staff bulletin board.
options.D: encrypt the data and limit access.

questions.explanation: Encrypt the data and limit access. Encryption scrambles data so it can't be read without a key, and limiting access means only employees who need the information can see it. Together, these steps reduce the risk of theft. Paper notebooks can be lost or copied, emailing card numbers exposes them to hackers, and posting them anywhere is a clear security violation. Businesses that accept cards must follow industry security standards, and a data breach can bring fines, lawsuits and lasting damage to a hotel's reputation.

performanceIndicator.text: Comply with strategies to protect digital customer data (e.g., information about customers, customers' credit-card numbers, passwords, customer transactions)

questions.question: A resort's department heads must agree on how to spend a $50,000 improvement budget. Housekeeping wants new carts, food and beverage wants patio heaters, and the spa wants new massage tables. Which approach best builds consensus?

options.B: Discuss each need and find a shared plan
options.C: Divide the money by drawing names
options.D: Let the general manager pick one department

questions.explanation: Discuss each need and find a shared plan. Consensus building brings people together to discuss their needs, priorities and trade-offs until they reach a plan everyone can support, perhaps funding the most urgent items now and others next year. Letting one person decide may be faster, but it doesn't build agreement. Drawing names ignores which needs matter most to guests and the business, and postponing indefinitely leaves every department without improvements. Managers who build consensus usually find that departments support the final plan more fully.

performanceIndicator.text: Use consensus-building skills

questions.question: A hotel's CRM system notes that a frequent guest is allergic to feathers, so housekeeping prepares her room with hypoallergenic pillows before each visit. This shows how CRM can

options.B: reduce the number of rooms sold.

questions.explanation: Personalize the guest experience. Customer relationship management systems store details about guests' preferences and needs so staff can personalize service. Preparing the guest's room with the right pillows before she arrives makes her feel valued and comfortable, which builds loyalty. CRM isn't meant to reduce rooms sold, replace housekeepers or raise prices. Hotels must be careful with personal information like allergies, sharing it only with employees who need it, but when used well, these records turn one-time guests into regulars.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of customer relationship management

questions.question: An HR manager at a resort is asked to share an employee's medical information with coworkers. The ethical response is to

options.A: post it on the staff bulletin board.
options.B: email it to the employee's team.
options.C: share it with everyone who asks.

questions.explanation: Keep the information confidential. Employees' medical information is private, and HR professionals have an ethical and often legal duty to protect it. Sharing it with coworkers, posting it or emailing it to a team could embarrass the employee, lead to unfair treatment and violate privacy laws. HR should share such information only when necessary and allowed, such as with a supervisor who needs to know about a work restriction, without revealing the diagnosis. Protecting confidentiality builds trust in HR across the whole organization.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the role of ethics in human resources management

questions.question: Which of the following is a current trend affecting how hospitality businesses hire and train employees:

options.D: Requiring all training to be in person

questions.explanation: Using online platforms for training. Many hotels and restaurants now use online training platforms and short videos that employees can complete on their phones or tablets, often during slow periods of a shift. This makes training faster, more consistent and easier to track. Requiring all training in person is becoming less common, ending training would hurt service quality, and most businesses hire throughout the year, not only in summer. Online training also makes it easier to update everyone quickly when a policy or menu changes.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe current business trends

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of preventing quality problems rather than fixing them after they happen:

options.A: Replacing a meal a guest sent back
options.D: Refunding a guest after a dirty stay

questions.explanation: Inspecting rooms before guests arrive. Prevention catches problems before guests experience them. Inspecting a room before a guest arrives allows housekeeping to fix missed spots, so the guest never sees them. Refunding a guest, answering a negative review and replacing a returned meal all happen after the guest has already had a bad experience. Those responses are still important, but prevention is usually cheaper and better for a business's reputation. Many hotels use inspection checklists so supervisors check the same items in every room.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of quality management

questions.question: Productivity in a restaurant kitchen increases when cooks

options.A: use more ingredients for each dish.
options.B: prepare more meals in the same time.
options.D: work longer hours for the same output.

questions.explanation: Prepare more meals in the same time. Productivity measures how much output is produced from a given amount of input, such as labor hours. When cooks prepare more meals in the same amount of time, productivity rises. Working longer for the same output lowers productivity, using more ingredients per dish raises costs without increasing output, and preparing fewer meals reduces output. Restaurants improve productivity with better kitchen layouts, prepping ingredients before busy periods, training and equipment that speeds up cooking without lowering quality.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of productivity

questions.question: A front desk clerk receives an email that appears to come from the hotel's IT department, asking her to click a link and enter her password to "verify her account." The email warns that her account will be locked within one hour if she doesn't respond. What should she do?

options.A: Click the link and enter her password
options.B: Forward the email to all coworkers
options.C: Reply with her password to save time
options.D: Report the email and not click the link

questions.explanation: Report the email and not click the link. Emails that ask for passwords through a link are a common phishing tactic used by criminals to steal login information and reach customer data. Real IT departments rarely ask employees to share passwords. The clerk should not click the link and should report the email to IT or her manager so others can be warned. Entering or replying with her password could give criminals access to guest records, and forwarding the email spreads the risk to coworkers who might fall for it. Urgent warnings like this one are a common sign of phishing.

performanceIndicator.text: Comply with strategies to protect digital customer data (e.g., information about customers, customers' credit-card numbers, passwords, customer transactions)

questions.question: A restaurant manager tells HR he wants to promote only servers under 30 because "younger people have more energy." What is the ethical issue?

options.B: It bases promotion on age, not ability
options.C: Older servers can't work evening shifts
options.D: Younger servers always earn more tips

questions.explanation: It bases promotion on age, not ability. Basing promotions on age rather than performance and skills is unfair, and for workers 40 and older it is illegal age discrimination under federal law. HR should explain the issue and help the manager use job-related criteria, such as performance reviews and leadership skills. Older servers can work evening shifts, promotions shouldn't be random, and the claim about tips is an unsupported assumption. Ethical HR practices protect employees from bias and protect the business from legal claims.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the role of ethics in human resources management

questions.question: A family checking into a resort asks for a crib and a room away from the elevator because their baby is a light sleeper. Which response best accommodates their request?

options.A: Suggest they bring their own crib next time
options.B: Charge them for a suite upgrade
options.C: Arrange both and confirm with them

questions.explanation: Arrange both and confirm with them. Accommodating guests' specific requests whenever possible makes them feel cared for and often earns loyalty. Arranging a crib and a quieter room, and confirming with the family, shows attentive service. Refusing all requests is poor service, charging for an upgrade they didn't ask for may feel unfair, and telling them to bring their own crib ignores a simple request most hotels can meet. Recording requests in the guest profile also helps staff remember the family's needs on future stays.

performanceIndicator.text: Accommodate special needs/specific requests of customers

questions.question: Hotel guests can now use smart speakers in their rooms to order towels or ask for restaurant hours. This technology mainly helps hotels
questions.explanation: Respond to requests quickly. Smart speakers let guests make simple requests by voice, any time of day, and send those requests directly to the right department, which speeds up service. They don't raise room rates, and while they reduce phone calls, they don't eliminate the need for front desk staff, who handle check-ins, problems and personal service. Room service continues; the speaker is simply another way to order it. Hotels must also protect guests' privacy when using voice technology, for example by deleting recordings after each stay.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain ways that technology impacts the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: A large rise in consumer spending on travel and dining usually signals that
questions.explanation: The economy is growing. Consumer spending makes up most of U.S. economic activity, so when people spend more, especially on extras like travel and dining, it usually means they feel confident about their jobs and income. That signals a growing economy. A recession usually brings lower spending, rising unemployment makes people cut back, and spending doesn't indicate that interest rates have hit zero. Hospitality businesses watch spending reports to plan staffing and inventory, since travel and dining are among the first purchases people cut in hard times.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the measure of consumer spending as an economic indicator

questions.question: A hotel recorded these nightly occupancy rates over five nights: 60%, 65%, 70%, 75% and 95%. Which statistic is least affected by the unusually high 95% night?
questions.explanation: The median. The median is the middle value when data are in order, which here is 70%. Because it depends only on the middle, one unusually high value barely affects it. The mean, (60 + 65 + 70 + 75 + 95) / 5 = 73%, is pulled upward by the 95% night. The range, 95% - 60% = 35%, depends directly on the highest value, and the maximum is the 95% night itself. Managers often use the median when a few unusual days, such as a holiday or event, would distort the average.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the use of descriptive statistics in business decision making

questions.question: Which of the following describes how mobile technology has changed the way many travelers choose restaurants while on vacation:

options.A: They eat only at their hotel
options.B: They check reviews on their phones
options.C: They rely only on printed guidebooks

questions.explanation: They check reviews on their phones. Smartphones let travelers search nearby restaurants, read reviews, look at photos and menus, and even book tables in seconds, often while walking down the street. Fewer travelers rely only on printed guidebooks, which can be out of date. Mobile technology encourages travelers to explore beyond their hotel and makes it easier to find authentic local food, not harder. For restaurants, this means online reviews, accurate hours and good photos on map apps can matter as much as a sign out front.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain ways that technology impacts the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: When two coworkers at a hotel disagree about how to divide holiday shifts, the best first step in resolving the conflict is to

options.A: give all the shifts to a third employee.
options.D: let each person explain his or her view.

questions.explanation: Let each person explain his or her view. Conflict resolution starts with understanding. Letting each person explain his or her view helps everyone see the full situation and often reveals solutions, such as trading shifts or alternating holidays each year. Deciding without discussion may leave both employees unhappy, telling them to stop complaining ignores the problem, and giving the shifts to a third person creates a new conflict. Managers who listen first usually find answers both people can accept and build trust for future disagreements.

performanceIndicator.text: Use conflict-resolution skill

questions.question: A restaurant's owner discovers that last month's food purchases were recorded twice in the accounting records. What is the most likely effect of this error?
questions.explanation: Reported expenses were too high. Recording the same purchases twice doubles those expenses in the records, so reported expenses are too high and reported profit is too low. Sales aren't affected because the error involved purchases, the restaurant's actual cash didn't increase, and financial reports, such as the income statement, will be wrong until the error is corrected. Mistakes like this show why accounting accuracy matters: managers could make poor decisions, such as cutting staff, based on a loss that doesn't really exist.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of accounting

questions.question: A restaurant manager who wants to know which menu items sell best should review
questions.explanation: Point-of-sale sales reports. Point-of-sale systems record every item sold, so their reports show exactly which dishes sell most and least. This internal information helps the manager decide which items to promote, change or remove. Competitors' menus and national statistics are external information that can't show what sells at this restaurant, and time cards track employees' hours rather than sales. Reviewing internal records regularly helps managers spot trends early, such as a dish that is losing popularity. Many systems also flag items that suddenly stop selling.

performanceIndicator.text: Monitor internal records for business information

questions.question: A ski resort invites a popular outdoor-adventure blogger to stay for free in exchange for an honest review. This promotional method is an example of
questions.explanation: Influencer marketing. Influencer marketing uses people with large, trusted audiences, such as bloggers and social media creators, to share a product with their followers. Their reviews can feel more believable than traditional ads. Direct mail sends printed materials to people's homes, personal selling involves one-on-one sales conversations, and price discounting lowers prices to encourage purchases. Businesses should require influencers to disclose free stays, because federal rules say audiences must be told when a review is sponsored.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain promotional methods used by the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: When building consensus on a new hotel uniform, a manager should

options.B: hold a vote and ignore the minority.
options.C: seek a choice everyone can support.
options.D: choose the uniform without asking anyone.

questions.explanation: Seek a choice everyone can support. Consensus building means working toward a decision that everyone can accept, even if it isn't each person's first choice. Asking for input, discussing concerns such as comfort and cost, and looking for a solution everyone can support leads to stronger buy-in. Deciding alone skips the process, letting the loudest person decide ignores others, and a simple vote that ignores the minority can leave some employees unhappy. Consensus takes longer than other methods, so it works best for decisions that affect many people.

performanceIndicator.text: Use consensus-building skills

questions.question: A hotel's housekeeping team includes employees who speak four different first languages. To help the team work well together, the manager should

options.A: assign each person to work alone.
options.C: require everyone to speak only during breaks.

questions.explanation: Translate key instructions. Translating important instructions, such as safety procedures and room-cleaning checklists, in employees' first languages or with pictures helps everyone understand expectations and work safely. Limiting conversation to breaks and assigning everyone to work alone would hurt teamwork and service, and ignoring language differences can lead to mistakes and frustration. Diverse teams can serve diverse guests better, since employees may be able to help international visitors in their own languages. Many hotels also offer language classes to employees who want to improve their English.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss issues associated with workplace diversity (e.g., ethnic, generational, religious, gender)

questions.question: Which of the following is the main reason a restaurant might assign each new server a "buddy" during the first two weeks of work:

options.A: To replace the restaurant's training program
options.B: To reduce the new server's pay
options.C: To provide a go-to person for questions
options.D: To keep the new server away from guests

questions.explanation: To provide a go-to person for questions. A buddy is an experienced coworker who helps a new employee learn routines, answers questions and makes introductions. This support helps new servers feel more comfortable and learn faster than they would on their own. Buddy programs don't reduce pay, keep new servers away from guests or replace formal training; they work alongside training. Restaurants that use buddy systems often see lower turnover, because new employees who feel supported in their first weeks are more likely to stay.

performanceIndicator.text: Orient new employees

questions.question: A theme park needs exactly 500 souvenir maps printed and delivered once before opening day. The park should use a
questions.explanation: Standard purchase order. A standard purchase order is used for a one-time purchase of specific items, quantities, prices and delivery dates, such as 500 maps delivered before opening day. A blanket purchase order covers repeated purchases from a supplier over a period, and a contract purchase order sets general terms with a supplier before specific orders are placed. A planned purchase order sets out expected purchases and future delivery dates in advance. Choosing the right type helps purchasing departments control spending and paperwork.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe types of purchase orders

questions.question: A hotel's purchasing department is responsible for

options.D: buying the goods the hotel needs.

questions.explanation: Buying the goods the hotel needs. Purchasing involves finding suppliers, comparing prices and quality, placing orders and making sure the hotel has the goods and services it needs, from linens and food to cleaning services. Room rates are usually set by revenue managers, hiring is handled by human resources, and advertising is a marketing task. Purchasing affects a hotel's costs and guest satisfaction, since poor-quality supplies or late deliveries can quickly lead to complaints. Good purchasing departments build strong relationships with reliable vendors.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature and scope of purchasing

questions.question: A hotel chain that redesigns its rooms after guests say they want more outlets and better lighting is performing
questions.explanation: Product/service management. Product/service management involves developing, maintaining and improving products and services to meet customer needs. Redesigning rooms based on guest feedback is a clear example. Financing involves obtaining and managing money, channel management involves the ways products reach customers, such as booking websites, and selling involves direct communication to persuade customers to buy. Hotels regularly update rooms because guests' expectations change, for example as they bring more devices that need charging. Product decisions also include which amenities to add or remove.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature and scope of the product/service management function

questions.question: A resort's accounting department records every payment it receives and makes. The main purpose of this work is to
questions.explanation: Provide accurate financial information. Accounting records, summarizes and reports a business's financial transactions, which gives managers, owners, lenders and tax authorities accurate information about its financial position. Marketing campaigns, housekeeping schedules and room rates are decided by other departments, although they often use accounting information to make those decisions. Without accurate records, a resort couldn't know its profit, prepare tax returns or spot problems such as rising costs. Accounting is often called the language of business for this reason.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of accounting

questions.question: While reviewing monthly reports, the manager of Driftwood Hotel notices that minibar revenue has dropped 40% even though occupancy is unchanged. What should she do next?

options.A: Ignore the change until next year
options.C: Raise minibar prices to cover the loss
options.D: Investigate the cause of the drop

questions.explanation: Investigate the cause of the drop. Internal records are valuable because they reveal unusual changes that need attention. A large drop in minibar revenue with steady occupancy suggests a specific cause, such as items not being restocked, a recording error, theft or guests buying snacks elsewhere. Investigating comes before acting. Removing minibars or raising prices may be the wrong response if the cause is a simple restocking problem, and ignoring the change could let losses continue. Monitoring records monthly lets managers catch problems while they are still small.

performanceIndicator.text: Monitor internal records for business information

questions.question: When a hotel guest complains that her room is noisy, the front desk agent should first

options.A: explain that all rooms are noisy.
options.D: ask her to call back tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Listen and apologize. Listening carefully and apologizing shows the guest that her concern matters and calms the situation. The agent can then offer a solution, such as a quieter room. Saying all rooms are noisy dismisses her complaint, asking her to call back delays help when she needs to sleep, and suggesting another hotel loses a customer. Handling complaints well can actually increase loyalty: guests whose problems are solved quickly often rate a hotel more highly than guests who never had a problem at all.

performanceIndicator.text: Handle customer/client complaints

questions.question: Lakeshore Hotel is choosing between two towel suppliers. Vendor A's towels cost 10% less, but samples became thin after 30 washes. Vendor B's towels cost more but stayed soft after 100 washes, and Vendor B offers free replacements for defects. Housekeeping replaces about 2,000 towels a year, and the hotel wants to keep its guest rating for room comfort above 4.5 stars. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.A: Vendor B may cost less over time
options.B: Price is the only factor that matters
options.C: Vendor A is always the better choice
options.D: The hotel should stop buying towels

questions.explanation: Vendor B may cost less over time. Evaluating vendors means looking at the total value, not just the price per item. Vendor A's towels wear out quickly, so the hotel would need to replace them much more often, which can make them more expensive over time. Vendor B's towels last longer and come with free replacements, which lowers long-term cost and keeps guests happier. Saying Vendor A is always better and that price is the only factor ignores durability, and the hotel can't stop buying towels. Testing samples is a smart way to compare vendors.

performanceIndicator.text: Evaluate vendors' goods and services

questions.question: Which of the following best uses digital media to improve a restaurant guest's experience after a meal:

options.A: A printed flyer mailed a year later
options.C: A radio ad for a competitor
options.D: A follow-up email asking for feedback

questions.explanation: A follow-up email asking for feedback. A follow-up email shortly after the visit thanks the guest and invites feedback, showing that the restaurant cares about the experience and wants to improve. If the guest had a problem, the restaurant can respond quickly. A printed flyer a year later isn't digital and arrives far too late, a billboard reaches the general public rather than past guests, and an ad for a competitor makes no sense. Restaurants often include a small offer in follow-up emails to encourage a return visit.

performanceIndicator.text: Use digital media to enhance customer post-sales experience

questions.question: A hotel guest who is traveling with a service dog asks whether the dog may stay in her room. The front desk agent should

options.A: place her in a separate building.
options.B: ask her to leave the dog in her car.
options.C: welcome the dog as the law requires.
options.D: charge her a large pet fee.

questions.explanation: Welcome the dog as the law requires. Under the Americans with Disabilities Act, hotels must generally allow service animals to accompany guests with disabilities, and they can't charge pet fees for service animals. Charging a pet fee, placing her in a separate building or asking her to leave the dog in her car would violate her rights and could put the animal at risk. Staff may ask only limited questions, such as whether the dog is required because of a disability and what task it has been trained to perform.

performanceIndicator.text: Accommodate special needs/specific requests of customers

questions.question: Which of the following is the main goal of customer relationship management for a restaurant:
questions.explanation: Building loyalty. CRM focuses on building lasting, profitable relationships by understanding customers and meeting their needs over time. Loyal guests visit more often, spend more and recommend the restaurant to others. Serving guests only once is the opposite of the goal, collecting data without using it wastes effort and creates privacy risks, and raising prices for loyal guests would push them away. Restaurants use CRM tools such as reservation histories and birthday offers to make guests feel recognized and appreciated.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of customer relationship management

questions.question: A restaurant group's economist reports that consumer spending has fallen for four straight months. Which of the following would be the most reasonable response for the group:

options.B: Plan carefully for a possible drop in sales
options.C: Ignore the report because restaurants are unaffected

questions.explanation: Plan carefully for a possible drop in sales. Falling consumer spending often signals that people are worried about the economy and cutting back, and dining out is one of the first expenses many households reduce. The group should plan for a possible decline, for example by controlling costs and preparing value promotions. Opening expensive new locations increases risk at a bad time, a big price increase could drive away remaining customers, and restaurants are strongly affected by spending trends. Economic indicators help businesses prepare instead of being surprised.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the measure of consumer spending as an economic indicator

questions.question: A hotel housekeeping team cleaned 90 rooms per shift last month. After switching to new cleaning carts that keep supplies organized, the same team now cleans 108 rooms per shift. By what percentage did productivity increase?
questions.explanation: 20%. Productivity increased by 108 - 90 = 18 rooms per shift. Dividing the increase by the original amount gives 18 / 90 = 0.20, or 20%. The answer 18% uses the number of extra rooms as a percentage, 10% and 8% don't come from these figures. The same team produces more output with the same labor, which is the definition of higher productivity. Small changes in tools or layout often raise productivity in hospitality, where many tasks are repeated dozens of times a day.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of productivity

questions.question: Which of the following would most likely cause a country's GDP to grow:

options.D: Consumers saving all of their income

questions.explanation: Businesses producing more. GDP rises when the economy produces more goods and services, for example when businesses expand, hire workers and serve more customers. If consumers saved all their income and spent nothing, businesses would sell less and production would fall. A sharp decline in tourism reduces spending at hotels, restaurants and attractions, and factory closings cut production. Economists watch GDP growth closely because it signals whether the economy is expanding, which usually means more jobs and higher incomes, or shrinking toward a recession.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of Gross Domestic Product (GDP)

questions.question: A guest at Ridgeway Inn complains at checkout that the Wi-Fi didn't work during his three-night business trip, which forced him to work from a coffee shop each evening. He asks the front desk agent what the hotel will do about it. Which response would best resolve the complaint?

options.A: Ask him to write an online review
options.B: Tell him the Wi-Fi is free anyway

questions.explanation: Apologize and offer a credit. The guest paid for a stay that included Wi-Fi and lost work time because it failed. Apologizing and offering a credit on his bill or toward a future stay acknowledges the problem and makes up for it. Saying the Wi-Fi is free dismisses its importance to business travelers, claiming no one else complained suggests he isn't believed, and asking for a review ignores his concern. The agent should also report the problem so it can be fixed before it affects other guests.

performanceIndicator.text: Handle customer/client complaints

questions.question: A restaurant manager wants to know the most common party size among her reservations last month. She should calculate the
questions.explanation: Mode. The mode is the value that appears most often in a set of data, so it shows the most common party size, such as tables of two. The mean is the average, which could be a size that rarely appears, such as 3.4 guests. The range is the difference between the largest and smallest values, and the total simply adds all guests together. Knowing the most common party size helps the manager arrange tables, for example by adding more two-person tables if couples make up most reservations.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the use of descriptive statistics in business decision making

questions.question: Seaview Resort agrees with a supplier on prices and payment terms for cleaning products for the coming year. It then places individual orders whenever supplies run low. Which of the following types of purchase orders is the resort using:
questions.explanation: Contract purchase order. A contract purchase order sets general terms, such as prices and payment conditions, with a supplier in advance, without specifying exact quantities or dates. The resort then places separate orders under that agreement as needed. A standard purchase order is a one-time order with set quantities and dates. Emergency and rush orders describe urgent purchases rather than a long-term agreement. Contract purchase orders save time and often lock in better prices, because the supplier expects steady business over the year.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe types of purchase orders

questions.question: Two servers at Bayview Bistro keep arguing about who should clean the coffee station at closing. Their arguments have started to slow down service during the evening rush, and two guests mentioned the tension in online reviews. Which solution would best resolve the conflict?

options.D: Stop serving coffee in the evening

questions.explanation: Create a rotating cleaning schedule. A rotating schedule gives each server a fair, clear turn, which removes the cause of the argument. Firing both servers is an extreme response that loses trained staff, letting the arguments continue keeps hurting service and teamwork, and ending evening coffee service punishes guests for an internal problem. Good conflict resolution focuses on the issue, not the people, and looks for solutions that feel fair to everyone involved. Writing the schedule down also prevents future disagreements about whose turn it is.

performanceIndicator.text: Use conflict-resolution skill

questions.question: Which of the following is a product/service management decision for a theme park:
questions.explanation: Adding a new family ride. Product/service management decides which products and services a business offers and how they change over time. Adding a new family ride changes what the park offers guests and is meant to attract new visitors and keep existing ones coming back. Choosing a bank, hiring an accountant and paying utilities are financial and administrative decisions, not product decisions. Theme parks invest heavily in new attractions because guests often choose where to visit based on what is new each season.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature and scope of the product/service management function

questions.question: A hotel owner who wants to know whether the hotel made a profit last year should review the
questions.explanation: Income statement. The income statement shows revenues and expenses over a period and the resulting profit or loss, so it answers the owner's question directly. Guest comment cards show satisfaction, the employee schedule shows who works when, and the marketing plan describes promotional goals, but none reports whether the business earned a profit. Accurate financial information is essential for decisions such as setting rates, controlling costs, hiring and applying for loans, which is why owners review financial statements regularly.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the need for financial information

questions.question: Which of the following is the main reason a bank needs a restaurant's financial statements before approving a loan to expand the dining room:

options.A: To judge its ability to repay
options.B: To choose the restaurant's new menu
options.C: To hire the restaurant's new staff
options.D: To set the restaurant's opening hours

questions.explanation: To judge its ability to repay. Lenders use financial information, such as revenue, expenses, profit and existing debt, to judge whether a borrower earns enough to make loan payments. Without accurate statements, the bank can't measure the risk of lending. The bank doesn't choose menus, set hours or hire staff; those are the owner's decisions. Restaurants that keep clear, accurate records are more likely to get loans and better interest rates, because lenders can see their financial health clearly. Banks may also ask for tax returns and cash flow projections.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the need for financial information

questions.question: Many restaurants now offer plant-based versions of popular dishes. This reflects a current business trend toward

options.B: serving fewer menu items each year.
options.D: replacing all restaurant workers with robots.

questions.explanation: Offering more sustainable menu items. Growing numbers of consumers want plant-based foods for health, environmental or ethical reasons, and restaurants are adding these options to attract and keep them. Replacing all workers with robots isn't a current trend, menus aren't consistently shrinking each year, and removing vegetarian dishes is the opposite of what is happening. Following trends like this helps businesses stay relevant. Restaurants that respond early can attract new customers, while those that ignore changing tastes may lose business to competitors.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe current business trends

questions.question: A few days after a cruise ends, the cruise line emails passengers a link to a photo gallery from their trip. This is an example of using digital media to

options.C: sell the passengers' photos to others.
options.D: reduce the cost of the cruise.

questions.explanation: Enhance the post-sales experience. The post-sales experience is everything a business does after a purchase to keep customers satisfied and connected. Sharing a photo gallery lets passengers relive their trip and share it with friends, which strengthens their good memories and may encourage another booking. Selling passengers' photos to others would violate their privacy, the email doesn't change the cost of the cruise, and it can't replace onboard activities. Digital follow-ups are inexpensive ways to build loyalty long after customers have gone home.

performanceIndicator.text: Use digital media to enhance customer post-sales experience

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a hotel using a loyalty program as a promotional method:

options.C: Painting the lobby a new color

questions.explanation: Awarding points. Loyalty programs reward repeat customers, often with points that can be used for free nights, upgrades or other perks. They encourage guests to keep choosing the same hotel brand instead of shopping around. Raising rates on busy weekends is a pricing decision, painting the lobby is a facility decision, and reducing staff is a staffing decision. Loyalty programs also give hotels valuable information about guests' preferences, which helps them personalize future promotions and service.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain promotional methods used by the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: When international tourists spend money at U.S. hotels and restaurants, that spending is counted in U.S. GDP because

options.A: tourism is excluded from all other measures.
options.B: the services are produced in the United States.
options.C: the tourists are citizens of other countries.
options.D: the money is converted from foreign currency.

questions.explanation: The services are produced in the United States. GDP measures the market value of final goods and services produced within a country's borders, no matter who buys them. Hotel stays and restaurant meals for foreign visitors are produced in the United States, so they count as part of U.S. GDP, specifically as exports of services. The tourists' citizenship doesn't determine whether spending counts, currency conversion isn't the reason, and tourism is included in other measures too, such as employment data. Tourism is a major source of GDP for many states, including Hawaii, Florida and Nevada.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of Gross Domestic Product (GDP)

questions.question: A well-planned orientation for new hotel employees mainly helps them

options.B: skip their first week of work.

questions.explanation: Learn policies and feel welcome. Orientation introduces new employees to the company's policies, procedures, facilities and people, which helps them feel welcome and confident sooner. Employees who understand expectations from the start make fewer mistakes and are more likely to stay. Orientation isn't a way to skip work, avoid coworkers or receive higher pay. Many hotels include a tour, introductions to team members, safety training and an explanation of guest-service standards, and some assign a mentor to answer questions during the first few weeks.

performanceIndicator.text: Orient new employees

questions.question: A restaurant that trains every cook to follow the same recipe and portion sizes is managing quality by
questions.explanation: Making results consistent. Quality management aims to deliver products that meet standards every time. When every cook follows the same recipe and portion sizes, guests get the same dish whether they visit on Monday or Saturday. Training doesn't require reducing the number of cooks, raising prices or shortening hours, though consistent portions can help control food costs. Consistency matters in hospitality because guests often return expecting the experience they had before, and a disappointing repeat visit can lose a customer for good.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of quality management

questions.question: A restaurant manager schedules all of the important religious holidays of one faith as paid days off but requires employees of other faiths to use vacation days for their holidays. Several employees have complained to HR about the policy. Which of the following describes the main issue:
questions.explanation: Unequal treatment of religious differences. Treating one religion's holidays more favorably than others' creates unequal treatment and can make employees feel excluded or disrespected. Employers are also legally required to make reasonable accommodations for employees' religious practices unless doing so would cause undue hardship. A fair approach might give every employee a set number of floating holidays to use as they choose. The issue isn't about a shortage of staff, overtime or uniforms. Fair policies help diverse teams trust management and work well together.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss issues associated with workplace diversity (e.g., ethnic, generational, religious, gender)

questions.question: When evaluating a new coffee supplier, a café owner should compare price along with
questions.explanation: Quality and reliability. A good vendor offers a fair price, consistent quality and reliable delivery. Cheap coffee that tastes poor or arrives late can cost more in lost customers than it saves. The supplier's office decor and website design say little about the products, and while a company's age can hint at stability, it matters much less than quality and reliability. Many businesses request samples, check references from other customers and review a vendor's delivery record before signing a contract.

performanceIndicator.text: Evaluate vendors' goods and services
